scenes.text: Many of today's biggest scams don't hack anyone. A fake bank officer, or a fake police call, talks the customer into sending the money themselves. Every security check passes, because the customer approved it. In India, citizens lost over twenty-two thousand crore rupees to cyber crime in 2024.

Last Mile Guard is a second look in the seconds before the money leaves. It checks the payment, reads the customer's own words with Gemini, and looks at the receiving account. Plain rules decide. A person confirms every hold. Everything you will see uses made-up data, and no money moves.

Here is the live site, running on Google Cloud. A customer is about to send ninety-eight thousand five hundred rupees, while a caller who says he is from the bank is on the line. I choose the bank-impersonation case and analyse the payment. Within seconds it is held, with a score from each of the three checks and a written reason for every point.

The customer sees a hold notice with a reference, and taps Call fraud team inside the app, so it cannot be a scammer's call. An AI agent asks two questions about this payment. Here the answers are typed. Gemini and Voice AI read them for coaching, secrecy and someone on the line, and recommend keeping the payment on hold. The case moves to the analyst, with the reasons, the call and the AI view in one place. The analyst keeps it on hold. Only a person can release a held payment.

We measured it, including the bad news. On a blind test of fifty cases written by someone else, the full system flagged eighty-four percent of scams. In the latest fresh run, thirty-eight of forty behaved as expected. Coached victims are the hardest: we caught three of five. Samples are small.
It runs on Google Cloud. Firebase Hosting sits in front of Cloud Run. Gemini on Vertex AI reads the words, with no keys in the code. Cases expire after twenty-four hours.
Last Mile Guard. A second look before the money moves.
